newsitem.title: UK: Liddell to up pressure on UK pension mis-selling.
newsitem.headline: Liddell to up pressure on UK pension mis-selling.

text.p: British Treasury Minister Helen Liddell is to increase pressure on insurance companies on Wednesday over compensating customers for pension mis-selling.

Liddell, who two weeks ago named two insurance companies she said had failed to understand the government's determination for a quick resolution, is to publish a "league table" showing how insurance companies are responding to the issue.
The details will be issued in a parliamentary written answer at around 1430 GMT.

Pension companies have been accused of persuading people to transfer from occupational pension schemes to inappropriate personal pension plans. The government says as many as half a million people may have been misadvised in the 1980s and 1990s.

Under pressure from the industry regulator, pension companies are now compensating victims of mis-selling. But many victims claim the process is taking too long and that many people have died before receiving any compensation. -- London Newsroom +44 171 542 7768
